claim: Transgenically expressed BirA biotinylates the bio epitope on Ep300fb, permitting quantitative Ep300 pull down on streptavidin beads.
source: Transgenically expressed BirA (Driegen et al., 2005) biotinylates the bio epitope, permitting quantitative Ep300 pull down on streptavidin beads (Figure 1C).
evidence: Figure 1C shows Western blot data demonstrating quantitative pulldown of biotinylated Ep300 by streptavidin beads, with GAPDH as a control.

claim: Ep300fb/fb hearts expressed normal levels of Ep300.
source: Ep300fb/fb hearts expressed normal levels of Ep300 and had normal size and function (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1B shows Western blot data comparing Ep300 expression levels between wild-type and Ep300fb/fb hearts.

claim: Ep300fb/fb hearts had normal size and function.
source: Ep300fb/fb hearts expressed normal levels of Ep300 and had normal size and function (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-E shows heart weight to body weight ratios and echocardiogram data demonstrating no significant differences between Ep300fb/fb and control mice.

claim: Ep300fb bioChIP-seq identified 48,963 Ep300-bound regions shared by both replicates in embryonic stem cells.
source: Ep300 bioChiP-seq identified 48963 Ep300-bound regions ('Ep300 regions') shared by both replicates, compared to 15281 for Ep300 antibody ChIP-seq (Figure 2A,C).
evidence: Figure 2A and 2C show Venn diagrams and heatmaps comparing the number of peaks detected by bioChIP-seq versus antibody ChIP-seq in ESCs.

claim: Ep300 antibody ChIP-seq identified 15,281 Ep300-bound regions shared by both replicates in embryonic stem cells.
source: Ep300 bioChiP-seq identified 48963 Ep300-bound regions ('Ep300 regions') shared by both replicates, compared to 15281 for Ep300 antibody ChIP-seq (Figure 2A,C).
evidence: Figure 2A and 2C show comparison data between bioChIP-seq and ENCODE antibody ChIP-seq methods.

claim: 89.6% of Ep300 regions detected by antibody ChIP-seq were also found by Ep300 bioChiP-seq.
source: The large majority (89.6%) of Ep300 regions detected by antibody were also found by Ep300 bioChiP-seq, and Ep300 signal was substantially stronger using bioChiP-seq (Figure 2A,C,D).
evidence: Figure 2A shows a Venn diagram demonstrating the overlap between antibody and bioChIP-seq detected regions.

claim: Ep300 signal was substantially stronger using bioChiP-seq compared to antibody ChIP-seq.
source: The large majority (89.6%) of Ep300 regions detected by antibody were also found by Ep300 bioChiP-seq, and Ep300 signal was substantially stronger using bioChiP-seq (Figure 2A,C,D).
evidence: Figure 2D shows correlation plots demonstrating greater signal intensity in bioChIP-seq compared to antibody ChIP-seq.

claim: Biological duplicate Ep300fb bioChIP-seq samples from E12.5 heart had 83% overlap.
source: There was high reproducibility (83% and 93%, respectively) between biological duplicates (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 3B shows Venn diagrams demonstrating overlap between biological replicates for heart and forebrain samples.

claim: Biological duplicate Ep300fb bioChIP-seq samples from E12.5 forebrain had 93% overlap.
source: There was high reproducibility (83% and 93%, respectively) between biological duplicates (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 3B shows Venn diagrams demonstrating overlap between biological replicates for heart and forebrain samples.

claim: Only 8.9% of heart Ep300fb regions were common between heart and forebrain tissues.
source: Only a minority of Ep300fb regions (8.9% for heart and 31.3% for brain) were common between tissues (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows a tag heatmap demonstrating tissue-specific Ep300 occupancy patterns.

claim: 31.3% of forebrain Ep300fb regions were common between heart and forebrain tissues.
source: Only a minority of Ep300fb regions (8.9% for heart and 31.3% for brain) were common between tissues (Figure 3A).
evidence: Figure 3A shows a tag heatmap demonstrating tissue-specific Ep300 occupancy patterns.

claim: Genes neighboring Ep300fb occupied regions specific to heart or forebrain were enriched for gene ontology functional terms relevant to the respective tissue.
source: Genes neighboring the Ep300fb occupied regions specific to heart or forebrain were enriched for gene ontology (GO) functional terms relevant to the respective tissue (Figure 3C).
evidence: Figure 3C shows GO biological process terms enriched for genes neighboring tissue-specific peaks, with statistical significance indicated.

claim: Ep300fb occupancy showed high correlation with H3K27ac in E12.5 heart and forebrain (r = 0.64).
source: Ep300 was also well correlated with H3K27ac (r = 0.64), independently validating the Ep300fb bioChIP-seq data.
evidence: The manuscript reports correlation analysis between Ep300fb bioChIP-seq and H3K27ac ChIP-seq data, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 130 out of 185 (70%) VISTA heart enhancers overlapped Ep300fb regions reproduced in both biological duplicates.
source: 185 tested regions had heart activity and 130 (70%) of these overlapped Ep300fb regions that were reproduced in both biological duplicates.
evidence: The manuscript compares Ep300fb bioChIP-seq regions to validated enhancers in the VISTA database.

claim: Only 105 out of 185 (57%) VISTA heart enhancers overlapped regions previously reported to be bound by Ep300 using antibody ChIP-seq.
source: In comparison, only 105 (57%) of these regions overlapped the regions previously reported to be bound by Ep300 using antibody ChIP-seq.
evidence: The manuscript compares antibody-based Ep300 ChIP-seq to VISTA validated enhancers.

claim: Ep300 bioChiP-seq was the single most predictive chromatin feature for heart enhancers with an AUC of 0.805.
source: This analysis showed that Ep300 bioChiP-seq was the single most predictive chromatin feature (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) = 0.805).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 3 shows ROC curves comparing different chromatin features for enhancer prediction using machine learning.

claim: ATAC-seq had an AUC of 0.749 for predicting heart enhancers.
source: ATAC-seq and H3K27ac also performed well (AUC = 0.749 and 0.747, respectively), whereas H3K4me1 had was poorly predictive (AUC = 0.589).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 3 shows ROC curves for different chromatin features.

claim: H3K27ac had an AUC of 0.747 for predicting heart enhancers.
source: ATAC-seq and H3K27ac also performed well (AUC = 0.749 and 0.747, respectively), whereas H3K4me1 had was poorly predictive (AUC = 0.589).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 3 shows ROC curves for different chromatin features.

claim: H3K4me1 was poorly predictive of heart enhancers with an AUC of 0.589.
source: ATAC-seq and H3K27ac also performed well (AUC = 0.749 and 0.747, respectively), whereas H3K4me1 had was poorly predictive (AUC = 0.589).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 3 shows ROC curves for different chromatin features.

claim: Combining Ep300 bioChIP-seq with ATAC-seq improved predictive accuracy to an AUC of 0.866.
source: Combining Ep300 bioChIP-seq with ATAC-seq improved predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.866), equivalent to the value obtained by performing predictions with all of the chromatin features (AUC = 0.862).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 3 shows ROC curves demonstrating improved prediction when combining features.

claim: Rosa26fsBirA expresses BirA in a Cre-dependent manner.
source: Thus, Rosa26fsBirA expresses BirA in a Cre-dependent manner.
evidence: Figure 4B shows Western blot demonstrating Cre-dependent Ep300 biotinylation, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A shows Cre-dependent BirA expression.

claim: 2,411 regions had enriched Ep300fb signal in Tie2Cre samples (Ep300-T-fb).
source: This led to the identification of 2411 regions with enriched signal in Tie2Cre (Ep300-T-fb) and 1292 regions with enriched signal in Myf5Cre (Ep300-M-fb), compared to 17382 regions with Ep300fb occupancy detected with ubiquitous biotinylation (Ep300-E-fb; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes filtering for lineage-selective regions based on signal ratios, with results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: 1,292 regions had enriched Ep300fb signal in Myf5Cre samples (Ep300-M-fb).
source: This led to the identification of 2411 regions with enriched signal in Tie2Cre (Ep300-T-fb) and 1292 regions with enriched signal in Myf5Cre (Ep300-M-fb), compared to 17382 regions with Ep300fb occupancy detected with ubiquitous biotinylation (Ep300-E-fb; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes filtering for lineage-selective regions based on signal ratios.

claim: 17,382 regions had Ep300fb occupancy detected with ubiquitous biotinylation (Ep300-E-fb).
source: This led to the identification of 2411 regions with enriched signal in Tie2Cre (Ep300-T-fb) and 1292 regions with enriched signal in Myf5Cre (Ep300-M-fb), compared to 17382 regions with Ep300fb occupancy detected with ubiquitous biotinylation (Ep300-E-fb; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript describes peak calling results from EIIaCre-driven bioChIP-seq.

claim: Ep300-T-fb regions were highly enriched for functional terms related to angiogenesis and hematopoiesis.
source: Ep300-T-fb regions were highly enriched for functional terms related to angiogenesis and hematopoiesis, whereas the Ep300-M-fb regions were highly enriched for functional terms related to skeletal muscle.
evidence: Figure 4F shows GO biological process terms enriched for genes neighboring lineage-specific Ep300 regions.

claim: Ep300-M-fb regions were highly enriched for functional terms related to skeletal muscle.
source: Ep300-T-fb regions were highly enriched for functional terms related to angiogenesis and hematopoiesis, whereas the Ep300-M-fb regions were highly enriched for functional terms related to skeletal muscle.
evidence: Figure 4F shows GO biological process terms enriched for genes neighboring lineage-specific Ep300 regions.

claim: 19 out of 40 (47.5%) validated endothelial cell enhancers from literature and VISTA database overlapped with Ep300-T-fb regions.
source: Of 40 positive regions identified, 19 (47.5%) overlapped with Ep300-T-fb regions.
evidence: The manuscript searched literature and VISTA database for validated EC enhancers and compared them to Ep300-T-fb regions, with results shown in Table 1.

claim: Out of 20 tested Ep300-T-fb regions, 8 drove reporter gene activity in at least three embryos in a vascular pattern.
source: Of the 20 tested Ep300-T-fb regions, eight drove reporter gene activity in at least three embryos in a vascular pattern, in both whole mounts and histological sections, and two additional regions drove reporter gene activity in a vascular pattern in two embryos (Figure 5B–D; Table 2; Figure 5—figure supplements 2–3).
evidence: Figure 5C-D and Table 2 show transient transgenic assay results for 20 tested regions.

claim: Two additional Ep300-T-fb regions drove reporter gene activity in a vascular pattern in two embryos.
source: Of the 20 tested Ep300-T-fb regions, eight drove reporter gene activity in at least three embryos in a vascular pattern, in both whole mounts and histological sections, and two additional regions drove reporter gene activity in a vascular pattern in two embryos (Figure 5B–D; Table 2; Figure 5—figure supplements 2–3).
evidence: Table 2 summarizes transient transgenic validation results.

claim: A substantial fraction (9/20; 45%) of regions identified by lineage-selective, Cre-directed bioChIP-seq have appropriate and reproducible in vivo activity.
source: Thus a substantial fraction (9/20; 45%) of regions identified by lineage-selective, Cre-directed bioChIP-seq have appropriate and reproducible in vivo activity.
evidence: The manuscript summarizes transient transgenic validation results showing 9 out of 20 tested regions had reproducible EC/blood activity.

claim: Sema6d-enh showed activity predominantly in ECs that line the dorsal aorta but not the cardinal vein.
source: We identified an enhancer, Sema6d-enh, with activity predominantly in ECs that line the dorsal aorta but not the cardinal vein (Figure 5E, Table 2).
evidence: Figure 5E shows histological sections demonstrating artery-selective activity of Sema6d-enh.

claim: Sox7-enh showed selective activity in the dorsal aorta, although this was only reproduced in two embryos.
source: A second enhancer, Sox7-enh, also showed selective activity in the dorsal aorta, although this was only reproduced in two embryos.
evidence: Table 2 shows Sox7-enh had activity in 2 out of 7 embryos with artery-selective pattern.

claim: Ephb4-enh and Mef2c-enh showed activity at E11.5 predominantly in ECs that line the cardinal vein and not the dorsal aorta.
source: We also identified two enhancers with activity at E11.5 predominantly in ECs that line the cardinal vein and not the dorsal aorta (Ephb4-enh and Mef2c-enh; Figure 5E, Table 2, and Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Figure 5E and Table 2 show vein-selective activity patterns for these enhancers.

claim: GATA and ETS motifs were the most highly enriched motifs in the Tie2Cre-marked blood and EC lineages.
source: The GATA and ETS motifs were the most highly enriched motifs in the Tie2Cre-marked blood and EC lineages (Figure 6A).
evidence: Figure 6A shows motif enrichment analysis with GATA and ETS motifs having the highest enrichment scores in Ep300-T-fb regions.

claim: The Ebox motif was the most highly enriched motif in the skeletal muscle lineage.
source: The Ebox motif, recognized by bHLH proteins, was the most highly enriched motif in the skeletal muscle lineage, consistent with the important roles of bHLH factors such as Myod and Myf5 in skeletal muscle development (Buckingham and Rigby, 2014).
evidence: Figure 6A shows motif enrichment analysis with Ebox having the highest enrichment in Ep300-M-fb regions.

claim: ETS:FOX2 heterodimer motif (AAACAGGAA) was highly enriched in Ep300-T-fb regions.
source: One heterodimer motif that was highly enriched in Ep300-T-fb regions (and not Ep300-M-fb regions; referred to as T2Cre-enriched motifs) was ETS:FOX2 (AAACAGGAA), comprised of a tail-to-tail fusion of Fox (TGTTT) and ETS (GGAA) binding sites (Figure 6A).
evidence: Figure 6A shows motif enrichment analysis identifying ETS:FOX2 as enriched in EC/blood enhancers.

claim: ETS:FOX2 motif was previously found to be sufficient to drive enhancer EC activity during vasculogenesis and developmental angiogenesis.
source: This motif was previously found to be sufficient to drive enhancer EC activity during vasculogenesis and developmental angiogenesis (De Val et al., 2008), validating that our approach is able to identify bona fide, functional heterodimer motifs.
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work by De Val et al., 2008 demonstrating the functional activity of this motif.

claim: ETS:FOX1 heterodimer motif (GGATGTT) was highly enriched in Ep300-T-fb regions.
source: Interestingly, we discovered two additional ETS-FOX heterodimer motifs, which were also highly enriched in Ep300-T-fb regions and also linked to vascular biological process terms: ETS:FOX1 (GGATGTT), consisting of a head-to-tail fusion between ETS and FOX motifs, with the ETS motif located 5' to the FOX motif (Figure 6A, arrows over motif logo), and ETS:FOX3 (TGTTTACGGAA), a head-to-tail fusion with the FOX motif located 5' to the ETS motif.
evidence: Figure 6A shows motif enrichment analysis identifying novel ETS:FOX heterodimer motifs.

claim: ETS:FOX3 heterodimer motif (TGTTTACGGAA) was highly enriched in Ep300-T-fb regions.
source: Interestingly, we discovered two additional ETS-FOX heterodimer motifs, which were also highly enriched in Ep300-T-fb regions and also linked to vascular biological process terms: ETS:FOX1 (GGATGTT), consisting of a head-to-tail fusion between ETS and FOX motifs, with the ETS motif located 5' to the FOX motif (Figure 6A, arrows over motif logo), and ETS:FOX3 (TGTTTACGGAA), a head-to-tail fusion with the FOX motif located 5' to the ETS motif.
evidence: Figure 6A shows motif enrichment analysis identifying novel ETS:FOX heterodimer motifs.

claim: Sequences matching Tie2Cre-enriched motifs within Ep300-T-fb regions showed a bimodal distribution of conservation scores including highly conserved sequences.
source: Whereas randomly selected 12 bp sequences from these regions exhibited a distribution of scores heavily weighted towards low conservation values, sequences matching Tie2Cre-enriched motifs showed a bimodal distribution consisting of highly conserved and poorly conserved sequences (Figure 6B).
evidence: Figure 6B shows PhastCons conservation score distributions comparing motif-matching sequences to random sequences.

claim: The ETS:FOX2 motif from an endothelial Mef2c enhancer robustly stimulated transcription to about the same extent as the SV40 enhancer in luciferase assays.
source: The well-studied ETS:FOX2 motif from an endothelial Mef2c enhancer (De Val et al., 2008) robustly stimulated transcription to about the same extent as the SV40 enhancer.
evidence: Figure 6C shows luciferase assay results demonstrating transcriptional activity of the ETS:FOX2 motif.

claim: Mutation of the ETS:FOX2 motif markedly blunted its transcriptional activity.
source: As expected, mutation of the ETS:FOX2 motif markedly blunted its activity, supporting the specificity of this assay.
evidence: Figure 6C shows luciferase assay results comparing wild-type and mutated ETS:FOX2 motifs.

claim: The ETS:FOX3 motif was at least as potent in stimulating transcription as the previously described ETS:FOX2 motif.
source: Interestingly, the alternative ETS:FOX3 motif uncovered by our study was at least as potent in stimulating transcription as the previously described ETS:FOX2 motif.
evidence: Figure 6C shows luciferase assay results comparing transcriptional activities of different ETS:FOX motifs.

claim: Both newly identified alternative ETS:FOX motifs (ETS:FOX1 and ETS:FOX3) were more potent activators than ETS:FOX2 when tested in a consistent DNA context.
source: Interestingly, both of the newly identified, alternative ETS:FOX motifs (ETS:FOX1 and ETS:FOX3) were more potent activators that ETS:FOX2.
evidence: Figure 6D shows luciferase assay results comparing motifs in a consistent DNA context.

claim: 240 genes were preferentially expressed in ECs from heart (and skeletal muscle) compared to other organs.
source: 240 genes were preferentially expressed in ECs from heart (and skeletal muscle) compared to other organs, whereas 355 genes were preferentially expressed in ECs from lung (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript analyzed published EC expression data from Nolan et al., 2013 to identify organ-specific EC genes.

claim: 355 genes were preferentially expressed in ECs from lung.
source: 240 genes were preferentially expressed in ECs from heart (and skeletal muscle) compared to other organs, whereas 355 genes were preferentially expressed in ECs from lung (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript analyzed published EC expression data to identify organ-specific EC genes, shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 14,251 regions were bound by Ep300fb in adult heart ECs.
source: To obtain a broader, unbiased view of the adult EC Ep300fb bioChIP-seq results, regions bound by Ep300fb in either heart (14251) or lung (22174) were rank-ordered by the heart to lung Ep300fb signal ratio (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports peak calling results from VEcad-CreERT2-driven bioChIP-seq in adult heart.

claim: 22,174 regions were bound by Ep300fb in adult lung ECs.
source: To obtain a broader, unbiased view of the adult EC Ep300fb bioChIP-seq results, regions bound by Ep300fb in either heart (14251) or lung (22174) were rank-ordered by the heart to lung Ep300fb signal ratio (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports peak calling results from VEcad-CreERT2-driven bioChIP-seq in adult lung.

claim: Genes neighboring decile 1 Ep300fb regions (greater signal in heart) had higher median mRNA transcript levels in heart than lung.
source: Genes neighboring decile one regions (greater Ep300fb signal in heart) had higher median mRNA transcript levels than lung (Figure 7B).
evidence: Figure 7B shows box plots comparing gene expression levels for genes neighboring different deciles of Ep300 regions.

claim: Genes neighboring decile 10 Ep300fb regions (greater signal in lung) had higher median mRNA transcript levels in lung than heart.
source: In contrast, genes neighboring decile 10 regions (greater Ep300fb signal in lungs) had higher median mRNA transcript levels in lung than heart.
evidence: Figure 7B shows box plots comparing gene expression levels for genes neighboring different deciles of Ep300 regions.

claim: More decile 1 Ep300fb regions were associated with genes with heart-selective expression than lung-selective expression (p<0.0001).
source: More decile 1 Ep300fb regions were associated with genes with heart-selective expression than lung-selective expression, and more decile 10 Ep300fb regions were associated with genes with lung-selective expression (in each case, p<0.0001, Fisher's exact test; Figure 7C).
evidence: Figure 7C shows the number of Ep300 regions in different deciles associated with organ-specific genes, with statistical significance indicated.

claim: More decile 10 Ep300fb regions were associated with genes with lung-selective expression (p<0.0001).
source: More decile 1 Ep300fb regions were associated with genes with heart-selective expression than lung-selective expression, and more decile 10 Ep300fb regions were associated with genes with lung-selective expression (in each case, p<0.0001, Fisher's exact test; Figure 7C).
evidence: Figure 7C shows the number of Ep300 regions in different deciles associated with organ-specific genes, with statistical significance indicated.

claim: Genes neighboring decile 1 regions (greater Ep300fb signal in heart) were significantly associated with coronary heart disease, arteriosclerosis, and myocardial infarction.
source: Analysis of disease ontology terms showed that genes neighboring decile one regions (greater Ep300fb signal in heart) were significantly associated with terms relevant to coronary artery disease, such as 'coronary heart disease', 'arteriosclerosis', and 'myocardial infarction', whereas genes neighboring decile 10 regions (greater Ep300fb signal in lung) were less enriched.
evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 4 shows disease ontology terms enriched in different deciles of Ep300 regions.

claim: Genes neighboring decile 10 regions (greater Ep300fb signal in lung) were selectively associated with hypertension and cerebral artery disease.
source: Conversely, genes neighboring decile 10 regions were selectively associated with hypertension and cerebral artery disease.
evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 4 shows disease ontology terms enriched in different deciles of Ep300 regions.

claim: The TCF motif was significantly enriched in regions preferentially occupied by Ep300 in heart ECs compared to lung ECs.
source: Using decile one regions as the foreground sequences and decile 10 regions as the background sequences, we detected significant enrichment of the TCF motif in regions preferentially occupied by Ep300 in heart ECs (Figure 7D), consistent with prior work that found that a Meox2:TCF15 complex promotes heart EC-specific gene expression (Coppiello et al., 2015).
evidence: Figure 7D shows motif enrichment analysis comparing heart and lung EC Ep300 regions.

claim: FOX, ETS, ETS-FOX and ETS-HOMEO motifs were significantly enriched in decile 1 (heart) compared to decile 10 regions.
source: Other motifs that were significantly enriched in decile 1 (heart) compared to decile 10 regions were FOX, ETS, ETS-FOX and ETS-HOMEO motifs.
evidence: Figure 7D shows motif enrichment analysis comparing heart and lung EC Ep300 regions.

claim: The TBOX motif was enriched in decile 10 (lung) compared to decile 1 regions.
source: One motif enriched in decile 10 (lung) compared to decile one regions was the TBOX motif.
evidence: Figure 7D shows motif enrichment analysis comparing heart and lung EC Ep300 regions.

claim: TBX3 is a lung EC-enriched transcription factor.
source: Interestingly, TBX3 is a lung EC-enriched transcription factor (Nolan et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites published expression data from Nolan et al., 2013.

claim: EBox, ETS:Ebox, and EBOX:HOMEO motifs were over-represented in decile 10 (lung) compared to decile 1 regions.
source: Other motifs over-represented in decile 10 compared to decile one regions were EBox, ETS:Ebox, and EBOX:HOMEO motifs.
evidence: Figure 7D shows motif enrichment analysis comparing heart and lung EC Ep300 regions.

claim: Most tissue-specific enhancers are bound by the transcriptional co-activator Ep300.
source: Since most tissue-specific enhancers are bound by the transcriptional co-activator Ep300, we used Cre-directed, lineage-specific Ep300 biotinylation and pulldown on immobilized streptavidin followed by next generation sequencing of co-precipitated DNA to identify lineage-specific enhancers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background for the study approach.

claim: Enhancers are nodal points of transcriptional networks, integrating multiple upstream signals to regulate gene expression.
source: Enhancers are nodal points of transcriptional networks, integrating multiple upstream signals to regulate gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: Enhancers do not have defined sequence or location with respect to their target genes.
source: Because enhancers do not have defined sequence or location with respect to their target genes, mapping enhancers is a major bottleneck for delineating transcriptional networks.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: DNase hypersensitivity has been used to identify cell-type-specific enhancers.
source: Recently chromatin immunoprecipitation of enhancer features followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) has been used to map potential enhancer. DNase hypersensitivity (Crawford et al., 2006; Thurman et al., 2012), H3K27ac (histone H3 acetylated on lysine 27) occupancy (Creyghton et al., 2010; Nord et al., 2013), or H3K4me1 (histone H3 mono-methylated on lysine 4) occupancy (Heintzman et al., 2007) are chromatin features that have been used to identify cell-type- specific enhancers.
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work using DNase hypersensitivity for enhancer identification.

claim: H3K27ac occupancy has been used to identify cell-type-specific enhancers.
source: Recently chromatin immunoprecipitation of enhancer features followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) has been used to map potential enhancer. DNase hypersensitivity (Crawford et al., 2006; Thurman et al., 2012), H3K27ac (histone H3 acetylated on lysine 27) occupancy (Creyghton et al., 2010; Nord et al., 2013), or H3K4me1 (histone H3 mono-methylated on lysine 4) occupancy (Heintzman et al., 2007) are chromatin features that have been used to identify cell-type- specific enhancers.
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work using H3K27ac for enhancer identification.

claim: H3K4me1 occupancy has been used to identify cell-type-specific enhancers.
source: Recently chromatin immunoprecipitation of enhancer features followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) has been used to map potential enhancer. DNase hypersensitivity (Crawford et al., 2006; Thurman et al., 2012), H3K27ac (histone H3 acetylated on lysine 27) occupancy (Creyghton et al., 2010; Nord et al., 2013), or H3K4me1 (histone H3 mono-methylated on lysine 4) occupancy (Heintzman et al., 2007) are chromatin features that have been used to identify cell-type- specific enhancers.
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work using H3K4me1 for enhancer identification.

claim: Most enhancers are DNase hypersensitive.
source: While most enhancers are DNase hypersensitive, DNase hypersensitive regions are often not active enhancers (Crawford et al., 2006; Thurman et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work characterizing the relationship between DNase hypersensitivity and enhancer activity.

claim: DNase hypersensitive regions are often not active enhancers.
source: While most enhancers are DNase hypersensitive, DNase hypersensitive regions are often not active enhancers (Crawford et al., 2006; Thurman et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work characterizing the limitations of DNase hypersensitivity for enhancer prediction.

claim: H3K27ac is enriched on cell type-specific enhancers.
source: H3K27ac is enriched on cell type-specific enhancers (Creyghton et al., 2010; Nord et al., 2013), but may be a less accurate predictor of enhancers than other transcriptional regulators (Dogan et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work characterizing H3K27ac enrichment at enhancers.

claim: H3K27ac may be a less accurate predictor of enhancers than other transcriptional regulators.
source: H3K27ac is enriched on cell type-specific enhancers (Creyghton et al., 2010; Nord et al., 2013), but may be a less accurate predictor of enhancers than other transcriptional regulators (Dogan et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work comparing the accuracy of different enhancer prediction methods.

claim: Ep300 is a transcriptional co-activator that catalyzes H3K27ac deposition.
source: Chromatin occupancy of Ep300, a transcriptional co-activator that catalyzes H3K27ac deposition, has been found to accurately predict active enhancers (Visel et al., 2009b).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work characterizing Ep300's enzymatic activity and role in enhancer prediction.

claim: Chromatin occupancy of Ep300 has been found to accurately predict active enhancers.
source: Chromatin occupancy of Ep300, a transcriptional co-activator that catalyzes H3K27ac deposition, has been found to accurately predict active enhancers (Visel et al., 2009b).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work by Visel et al., 2009b demonstrating Ep300's utility for enhancer prediction.

claim: Antibodies for Ep300 are marginal for robust ChIP-seq, particularly from tissues.
source: However, antibodies for Ep300 are marginal for robust ChIP-seq, particularly from tissues, leading to low reproducibility, variation between antibody lots, and inefficient enhancer identification (Gasper et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work documenting limitations of Ep300 antibodies for ChIP-seq.

claim: Ep300 antibodies lead to low reproducibility, variation between antibody lots, and inefficient enhancer identification.
source: However, antibodies for Ep300 are marginal for robust ChIP-seq, particularly from tissues, leading to low reproducibility, variation between antibody lots, and inefficient enhancer identification (Gasper et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work documenting problems with Ep300 antibody-based ChIP-seq.

claim: Heart development and function are sensitive to Ep300 gene dosage.
source: Heart development and function are sensitive to Ep300 gene dosage (Shikama et al., 2003; Wei et al., 2008), yet Ep300fb/fb homozygous mice survived normally (Figure 1D) and Ep300fb/fb hearts expressed normal levels of Ep300 and had normal size and function (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work demonstrating Ep300 dosage sensitivity in heart development.

claim: GATA1/2/3 have critical roles in hematopoiesis and heme synthesis.
source: Interestingly, GO analysis of the subset of regions positive for these motifs showed that GATA-containing regions are highly enriched for hematopoiesis and heme synthesis, consistent with the critical roles of GATA1/2/3 in these processes (Bresnick et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on GATA factors' roles in hematopoiesis.

claim: ETS factors have key roles in angiogenesis.
source: On the other hand, ETS-containing regions were highly enriched for functional terms linked to angiogenesis, also consistent with the key roles of ETS factors in angiogenesis (Wei et al., 2009) and our prior finding that the ETS motif is enriched in dynamic VEGF-dependent EC enhancers (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on ETS factors' roles in angiogenesis.

claim: bHLH factors such as Myod and Myf5 have important roles in skeletal muscle development.
source: The Ebox motif, recognized by bHLH proteins, was the most highly enriched motif in the skeletal muscle lineage, consistent with the important roles of bHLH factors such as Myod and Myf5 in skeletal muscle development (Buckingham and Rigby, 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on bHLH factors' roles in muscle development.

claim: bHLH-encoding genes such as Hey1/2, Scl, and Myc are important in blood and vascular development.
source: bHLH-encoding genes such as Hey1/2, Scl, and Myc are known to be important in blood and vascular development.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge without specific citation.

claim: ECs in different adult organs have distinct gene expression programs that underlie organ-specific EC functions.
source: ECs in different adult organs have distinct gene expression programs that underlie organ-specific EC functions (Nolan et al., 2013; Coppiello et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work characterizing organ-specific EC gene expression.

claim: Heart ECs are adapted for the transport of fatty acids essential for fueling oxidative phosphorylation in the heart.
source: For example, heart ECs are adapted for the transport of fatty acids essential for fueling oxidative phosphorylation in the heart (Coppiello et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on heart EC specialization.

claim: Lung ECs are adapted for efficient transport of gas but possess specialized tight junctions to minimize transit of water.
source: On the other hand, lung ECs are adapted for efficient transport of gas, but possess specialized tight junctions to minimize transit of water (Mehta et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on lung EC specialization.

claim: Meox2 has been implicated in directing expression of heart EC-specific genes.
source: Interestingly, Meox2 has been implicated in directing expression of heart EC-specific genes and in the pathogenesis of coronary artery disease (Coppiello et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on Meox2's role in heart EC gene expression.

claim: Meox2 has been implicated in the pathogenesis of coronary artery disease.
source: Interestingly, Meox2 has been implicated in directing expression of heart EC-specific genes and in the pathogenesis of coronary artery disease (Coppiello et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on Meox2's role in coronary artery disease.

claim: A Meox2:TCF15 complex promotes heart EC-specific gene expression.
source: Using decile one regions as the foreground sequences and decile 10 regions as the background sequences, we detected significant enrichment of the TCF motif in regions preferentially occupied by Ep300 in heart ECs (Figure 7D), consistent with prior work that found that a Meox2:TCF15 complex promotes heart EC-specific gene expression (Coppiello et al., 2015).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on the Meox2:TCF15 complex.

claim: Ep300fb bioChIP-seq has improved sensitivity compared to Ep300 antibody ChIP-seq for mapping Ep300 chromatin occupancy in cultured cells.
source: These data indicate that Ep300fb bioChiP-seq has improved sensitivity compared to Ep300 antibody ChIP-seq for mapping Ep300 chromatin occupancy in cultured cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the comparison data shown in Figure 2, demonstrating more peaks and better reproducibility with bioChIP-seq.

claim: The epitope-tagged Ep300fb allele has superior sensitivity and specificity for mapping Ep300-bound regions in tissues compared to antibody-based methods.
source: These regions overlapped 58.7% and 64.7% of the Ep300fb bioChIP-seq regions, suggesting that the epitope-tagged allele has superior sensitivity and specificity for mapping Ep300-bound regions in tissues, as it does in cultured cells.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from comparison of bioChIP-seq to antibody ChIP-seq in heart and forebrain tissues.

claim: Ep300 occupies tissue-specific enhancers.
source: These results reinforce the conclusion that Ep300 occupies tissue-specific enhancers and indicate that this conclusion was not a consequence of insensitive detection of Ep300-occupied regions in earlier studies (Visel et al., 2009b).
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the tissue-specific patterns of Ep300 occupancy shown in Figure 3A and genome browser views in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Ep300fb occupancy is more tissue-specific than H3K27ac occupancy.
source: Interestingly, 26.4% and 52.9% of heart and brain H3K27ac regions were shared between tissues (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D) compared to 8.9% and 31.3% for Ep300fb heart and brain regions, respectively (Figure 3A), suggesting that Ep300fb occupancy is more tissue-specific.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from comparing the overlap percentages between tissues for Ep300fb versus H3K27ac.

claim: Ep300fb ChIP-seq predicts heart enhancers with sensitivity that is superior to antibody-mediated Ep300 ChIP-seq.
source: We conclude that Ep300fb ChIP-seq predicts heart enhancers with sensitivity that is superior to antibody-mediated Ep300 ChIP-seq.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from multiple validation experiments comparing bioChIP-seq to antibody ChIP-seq, including VISTA enhancer overlap and literature-validated enhancers.

claim: Ep300 is the best single factor for enhancer prediction among the chromatin features tested.
source: These analyses indicate that of the features tested Ep300 is the best single factor for enhancer prediction.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from machine learning analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3 comparing AUC values for different chromatin features.

claim: Cre-driven, lineage-specific Ep300fb bioChIP-seq successfully identifies regulatory regions associated with lineage relevant biological processes.
source: Together, these results indicate that our strategy for Cre-driven, lineage-specific, Ep300fb bioChiP-seq successfully identifies regulatory regions that are associated with lineage relevant biological processes.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from GO analysis shown in Figure 4F demonstrating enrichment of lineage-appropriate terms.

claim: Ep300-T-fb regions are enriched for enhancers that are active in the Tie2Cre-labeled lineage.
source: Together, our data are consistent with Ep300-T-fb regions being enriched for enhancers that are active in the Tie2Cre-labeled lineage.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from TRAP RNA-seq analysis showing higher expression of genes neighboring Ep300-T-fb regions in Tie2Cre-labeled cells.

claim: A majority of candidate enhancers identified by lineage-selective bioChIP-seq are expected to have in vivo, cell-type specific transcriptional enhancer activity.
source: Based on our validation studies, we expect that a majority of these candidate regions have in vivo, cell-type specific transcriptional enhancer activity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from transient transgenic validation showing 45% of tested regions had reproducible activity, plus literature validation showing 47.5% overlap.

claim: Novel heterodimer motifs identified in this study are likely functional in endothelial cells.
source: Enrichment of these motifs in Ep300-T-fb, and their over-representation neighboring genes related to angiogenesis, suggests that these alternative FOX-ETS configurations are functional.
evidence: This inference is drawn from motif enrichment analysis, conservation analysis, and luciferase assays demonstrating transcriptional activity.

claim: Differences in transcription factor expression or heterodimer formation in heart and lung ECs may contribute to differences in Ep300 chromatin occupancy and enhancer activity between heart and lung.
source: Thus differences in transcription factor expression or heterodimer formation in heart and lung ECs may contribute to differences in Ep300 chromatin occupancy and enhancer activity between heart and lung.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from motif enrichment analysis showing differential enrichment of specific motifs in heart versus lung EC Ep300 regions.

claim: Cell type-specific protein biotinylation will be useful for mapping protein-protein interactions in specific cell lineages.
source: Cell type-specific protein biotinylation will also be useful for mapping protein-protein interactions in specific cell lineages.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications of the technology.

claim: Large scale identification of tissue-specific enhancers will facilitate decoding the mechanisms responsible for cell type-specific gene expression in development and disease.
source: Large scale identification of tissue-specific enhancers will facilitate decoding the mechanisms responsible for cell type-specific gene expression in development and disease.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about the impact of the work.

claim: The ETS motif is enriched in dynamic VEGF-dependent EC enhancers.
source: On the other hand, ETS-containing regions were highly enriched for functional terms linked to angiogenesis, also consistent with the key roles of ETS factors in angiogenesis (Wei et al., 2009) and our prior finding that the ETS motif is enriched in dynamic VEGF-dependent EC enhancers (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work by the authors on ETS motif enrichment in VEGF-dependent enhancers.

claim: Ep300 decorates many, but not all, active transcriptional enhancers.
source: Another limitation of our strategy is that Ep300 decorates many, but not all, active transcriptional enhancers (He et al., 2011), and therefore Ep300 bioChIP-seq will not comprehensively detect all enhancers.
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work and acknowledges this as a limitation of the approach.

claim: The bio epitope has been knocked into a number of different transcription factor loci.
source: The bio epitope has been knocked into a number of different transcription factor loci (He et al., 2012; Waldron et al., 2016) and Jackson Labs 025982 (Rbpj), 025980 (Ep300), 025983 (Mef2c), 025978 (Nkx2-5), 025979 (Srf), and 025977 (Zfpm2)), and these alleles can be combined with Cre-activated BirA to permit lineage-specific mapping of transcription factor binding sites.
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work and lists available mouse lines with bio-tagged transcription factors.

claim: Only three artery-specific and no vein-specific transcriptional enhancers have been described prior to this study.
source: Arterial and venous ECs have overlapping but distinct gene expression programs, yet only three artery-specific and no vein-specific transcriptional enhancers have been described (Wythe et al., 2013; Robinson et al., 2014; Becker et al., 2016; Sacilotto et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior literature on artery and vein-specific enhancers.

claim: A core 44-bp region of Mef2c-enh had been previously reported to drive pan-EC reporter expression at E8.5–E9.5.
source: Interestingly, a core 44-bp region of Mef2c-enh had been previously reported to drive pan-EC reporter expression at E8.5–E9.5 (De Val et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on the Mef2c enhancer.

claim: Some enhancers' activity patterns may be dynamically regulated at different developmental stages.
source: This enhancer's activity pattern may be dynamically regulated at different developmental stages, as has been described previously for two artery-specific enhancers (Robinson et al., 2014; Becker et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work showing temporal regulation of enhancer activity.

claim: Optimization of chromatin pulldown and purification through streamlined protocols or microfluidics will likely overcome the limitation of needing several million cells.
source: Optimization of chromatin pulldown and purification through application of streamlined protocols or microfluidics (Cao et al., 2015), combined with the use of improved library preparation methods that work on smaller quantities of starting material, will likely overcome this limitation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future improvements to the method.

claim: The lineage specificity of the technique is dependent on the properties of the Cre allele used.
source: Finally, our technique's lineage specificity is dependent on the properties of the Cre allele used (Ma et al., 2008), and users must be cognizant of the cell labeling pattern of the Cre allele that they choose.
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work on Cre allele properties and notes this as a consideration for users.
